account: Tokyo-based Asilla's system assesses the likelihood that a person will jump by analyzing behavior on security-camera footage. Asilla says that it has trained the system since 2022 with around 200 facilities on about seven million pieces of footage. Its product release of 26 January 2024 identifies a jump-risk detection function in AI Security asilla version 2.4, using movement trajectories, position, and body-motion patterns. The system looks for behavior such as pacing or lingering near a platform edge or rooftop. It alerts security guards and station staff, in some cases with loudspeaker warnings. Kyodo reported on 1 June 2026 that Asilla described two interventions, both undated. In one case the system detected a man loitering in a non-customer area of a commercial facility. A guard found him, and he later said that he had intended to kill himself by jumping. In another, a child lingering near an upper-floor railing was found to have been writing a suicide note. The product release does not identify the version used in these two interventions. All details come from the company via Kyodo, and no operator, police or academic confirmation is among the sources. In Stockholm, Karolinska Institutet researchers reported in July 2026 that suicide-related incidents on the tracks fell at 14 metro stations after an AI camera system was installed in late 2021, compared with 86 other stations. They studied a different system and did not test Asilla's.

fields.account: Tokyo-based Asilla's system assesses the likelihood that a person will jump by analyzing behavior on security-camera footage. Asilla says that it has trained the system since 2022 with around 200 facilities on about seven million pieces of footage. Its product release of 26 January 2024 identifies a jump-risk detection function in AI Security asilla version 2.4, using movement trajectories, position, and body-motion patterns. The system looks for behavior such as pacing or lingering near a platform edge or rooftop. It alerts security guards and station staff, in some cases with loudspeaker warnings. Kyodo reported on 1 June 2026 that Asilla described two interventions, both undated. In one case the system detected a man loitering in a non-customer area of a commercial facility. A guard found him, and he later said that he had intended to kill himself by jumping. In another, a child lingering near an upper-floor railing was found to have been writing a suicide note. The product release does not identify the version used in these two interventions. All details come from the company via Kyodo, and no operator, police or academic confirmation is among the sources. In Stockholm, Karolinska Institutet researchers reported in July 2026 that suicide-related incidents on the tracks fell at 14 metro stations after an AI camera system was installed in late 2021, compared with 86 other stations. They studied a different system and did not test Asilla's.

echoes.setting: Stockholm metro, Sweden: an AI-CCTV detection system installed at 14 stations in late 2021; Karolinska Institutet researchers found that suicide-related incidents on the tracks fell compared with 86 other stations (IRR 0.27)

purpose: Detect behavior indicating suicide risk (and illness, immobility or violence) in security-camera footage and alert staff.

ratings.reason: Guards reached two people in apparent crisis after alerts, according to the developer. The sources contain no independent account of either case.
The sources contain no outcome reported by an operator and no data on false alerts.

summary: Asilla's behavior-analysis AI for security cameras alerted guards, who then reached two people at apparent risk of suicide, the company says; the facilities and dates are undisclosed.
system: Asilla AI behavior-analysis system for security cameras
